text:
Alex Nguyen: Heads up — nightly h100 CI just went red on the 'llm-inference' matrix (shard 7). Failure is a mix of persistent OOM and a kernel error: Xid=31 then later `invalid device function`. Only failing on h100 nodes after the driver bump. Anyone seen this pattern after the recent infra deploy?

Maria Gomez: which test? quick paste of the top log lines would help. is it quant-attn or something I/O heavy?

Alex Nguyen: test name: tests/inference/test_attention_cache.py::test_long_prefix_load
Log snippet: ```
E tensorflow: cudaLaunchKernel returned 999 (invalid device function)
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 31, PID 22111
GPU0: out-of-memory while allocating 9.0 GiB
```

Chen Li: invalid device function + Xid can mean PTX/jit vs driver mismatch. We recently moved to a new container runtime build with cudatoolkit 12.2 artifacts while infra driver bumped to 535.54. If the node has a different driver (or leftover module) you can see this.

Samir Patel: I'll kick a debug rerun on that shard with env overrides. @ci-bot can you re-run job (shard 7) with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and NV_DEBUG=1 and pin DRIVER=535.86 for comparison? Also collect dmesg and /var/log/messages.

ci-bot: Rerun requested: job_id=#4921, shard=7, env_overrides={CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1,NV_DEBUG=1,DRIVER=535.86}. Debug artifacts harvest enabled. ETA ~15m.

ci-bot: Rerun finished: status=failed. Attaching short artifact: ```
/var/log/dmesg: [   45.123456] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3d:00): 79, PID 33445: GPU has fallen off the bus
[   45.123789] NVRM: GPU reset
/ci/artifacts/test_log.txt: cudaLaunchKernel returned 999 (invalid device function)
```

Maria Gomez: Xid=79 / fallen off the bus + reset suggests kernel module mismatch or unstable PCI link. Can you run `nvidia-smi -a` and `modinfo nvidia` on the host that executed the job?

Alex Nguyen: Pasted from the failing host (trimmed): ```
$ nvidia-smi -a | head -n 8
Product Name: H100-SXM
Driver Version: 535.54
CUDA Version: 12.2
Attached GPUs : 1

$ modinfo nvidia | grep version
version: 535.54
srcversion: ABCDEF1234
```

Chen Li: that looks consistent on that node, but ci-bot artifact shows Xid=79 then 31. Could be transient firmware mismatch or a background driver roll that left some nodes with 535.86 and others at 535.54. Kernel module ABI mismatch can cause invalid device function when JIT-ed kernels expect different PTX.

Samir Patel: Proposing a quick bisect: revert the runtime-lib bump (commit abc1234) that changed the built PTX to confirm. Alternatively, Infra can repro with pinned older driver on a fresh host. What does infra want?

Chen Li: I can try a small local repro matrix: build the container with both cudatoolkit=12.1 and 12.2 and run the failing test against both driver versions in a lab node. If we see deterministic mismatch, we can blame the runtime build.

Alex Nguyen: Assigning: @Chen Li to run the two-build repro and report, @Samir Patel to collect full host logs and upload to S3 (path: s3://redwood-ci/bugs/1712349999/), @Infra Oncall to isolate a failing node and repro with driver 535.54 rollback. I'll open an incident ticket with notes.

Infra Oncall: ACK. I'll cordon the node, repro with driver 535.54 and then try 535.86 on a clean repro. If we see the same failure under 535.54, we'll look at firmware. ETA ~1h.

ci-bot: Artifact upload completed: s3://redwood-ci/bugs/1712349999/artifacts.tar.gz (logs + dmesg + nvidia-smi snapshots).

Chen Li: Quick update: local matrix showstest_long_prefix_load passes against driver 535.54 but fails under 535.86 when built with cudatoolkit 12.2 containers. Repro is small but consistent. Likely the runtime's compiled kernels are not fully compatible with the newer driver PTX expectations. I'll start a bisect on the runtime-tooling commits (starting point abc1234 -> head).

Alex Nguyen: Great — thanks. I'm filing incident INC-2026-19 with the above train-of-thought and linking the artifacts. Will escalate to runtime and infra teams if bisect points to a build change.

Samir Patel: FYI I left the node cordoned and saved the full /var/crash bundle at s3://redwood-ci/bugs/1712349999/host_bundle.tar.gz

Maria Gomez: pinging runtime-team for visibility: @Chen Li please @runtime-team when you have the bisect results. Also consider a temporary test skip on shard 7 for nightly until we have a root cause to avoid noise.

Alex Nguyen: Agree on temporary skip if it keeps nightly green for other teams. Will coordinate with CI config owners. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
